chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Abbas Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hammad narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id Yahya ibn Hakim narrated to us, he said: Abu Qutayba narrated to us, he said: Al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Rafi', from Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his fathers (peace be upon them), from Fatima, daughter of the Prophet (peace be upon them both), that she said:

I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) say: Indeed, on Friday there is an hour that a Muslim man does not observe while asking Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, for goodness, except that He will give it to him. She said: Then I said: O Messenger of Allah, what hour is it? He said: When the half of the sun's eye sinks down for sunset. He said: And Fatima (peace be upon her) used to say to her servant: Climb on the elevated rock, and if you see that half of the sun's eye has sunk for sunset, notify me so that I may supplicate.

key_terms.الضَّرَابِ: The elevated rock or high place
key_terms.عَيْنِ الشَّمْسِ: The eye of the sun (a poetic reference to the sun's position)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific time on Friday when prayers are accepted according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* underscores the spiritual potency of the 'hour of acceptance' on Friday, linking it to the precise moment of sunset. Her practical method of using a servant to monitor the sun from an elevated position highlights the scholarly emphasis on exact timing (*waqt*) in Shia jurisprudence for maximizing the efficacy of supplication. This specific window is traditionally viewed as a time when divine response is imminent due to the convergence of the day's conclusion and the transition to the next.

en.basel-kadem: 57. We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Abu’l-Abbas, Abdul-Rahman bin Muhammed bin Hammad, that he said: We were told by Abu Sa’eed, Yahya bin Hukaim, that he said: We were told by Abu Qutayba, that he said: We were told by Asbagh bin Zaid, from Sa’eed bin Rafe’, from Zaid bin Ali (a.s) from his fathers, peace be upon them, from Fatima, daughter of the Prophet (sa) that she said:

I heard the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, say: Indeed, on Friday there is an hour that is not observed by a Muslim man in which he asks Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, for goodness, except that He will give it to him. She said: Then I said: O Messenger of Allah, what hour is it? He said: When the half of the sun’s eye sinks down for sunset. He said: Fatima (sa) used to say to her servant: Climb on the elevated rock, and if you see that half of the sun’s eye has sunken for sunset, notify me that I may supplicate.
